key_findings: Eliminated verbose outputs (>80 words): 19.5% base → 0.0% fine-tuned
Perfect format discipline: 100% capital-letter starts, 0% markdown fences
Learned appropriate conciseness: 79% one-liners vs 19% for base model
Lower Google-section rate reflects learned conciseness matching training distribution
notes: Evaluation on 200 randomly sampled held-out test examples from the 1,249-example test split. The fine-tuned model shows hallucination elimination and improved format discipline. The lower Google-style section rate (15.5% vs 78.5% base) reflects learned conciseness — the model correctly produces one-liners for simple functions and structured sections for complex ones, matching the training data distribution. This is appropriate behavior, not a regression.
